adjustment.analysis: No events or price changes in the target week. The classical uplift model suggests a 18% downside from the prior promotion (2026-06-01), but the noise-adjusted effect of 'week after promotion' is x0.82, which is already conservative. The past Father's Day effect is noise-adjusted x1.0, so no uplift. The 20% off promotion on 2026-06-01 drove a 65% lift, but the model's prior-week adjustment accounts for the pull-forward. No other drivers. The baseline trend is strong (47.6% 13-week trend), but already reflected. Keep median at baseline. Spreads remain unchanged.

  shelf price: 12.21 (+0.0% vs regular price 12.21)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 204.0 | 5%-95%: 131.7 - 272.4 | 10%-90%: 151.1 - 246.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-33% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
